title: Circumference and Pi: Radius, Diameter and C = πd
seo_title: Year 7 Circumference Worksheets: Parts of a Circle, Pi and C = πd (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: describe the relationship between π and the features of circles including the circumference, radius and diameter
meta_desc: Free Year 7 maths worksheets on circumference and π for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M7M03): parts of a circle, radius and diameter, why C ÷ d = π, finding the circumference and working backwards. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: For every circle, circumference ÷ diameter = π ≈ 3.14.
body_html:
How it works

The radius r goes from the centre to the edge. The diameter d = 2r goes right across. The circumference C is the distance all the way round.

For every circle, circumference ÷ diameter = π (about 3.14). So C = πd, or C = 2πr. Use the π button on a calculator and round at the end, or leave the answer in terms of π, such as 8π cm.

Example

Find the circumference of a circle with diameter 8 cm.

π × 8 = 25.13…

Answer: 25.1 cm

Example

Find the circumference of a circle with radius 5 cm.

2 × π × 5 = 10π = 31.41…

Answer: 31.4 cm

Example

A circle has circumference 40 cm. Find its diameter.

40 ÷ π = 12.73…

Answer: 12.7 cm

Common mistakes

  • Using the radius in C = πd. With r = 5, the diameter is 10.
  • Doubling twice: if you use the diameter, do not multiply by 2 as well.
  • Multiplying by π when working backwards. To find d, divide C by π.
  • For a semicircle's perimeter, forgetting to add the straight diameter.

faq.a: π is the circumference of any circle divided by its diameter. It is about 3.14159 and its decimals never end.

faq.q: What is the formula for circumference?
faq.a: C = πd, or C = 2πr, because the diameter is twice the radius.

faq.q: How do I find the diameter from the circumference?
faq.a: Divide the circumference by π. A circle with C = 31.4 cm has d ≈ 10 cm.

faq.q: What is the difference between radius and diameter?
faq.a: The radius goes from the centre to the edge. The diameter goes right across through the centre, so d = 2r.
